title: XRAG: Cross-lingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Wei Liu; Sony Trenous; Leonardo F. R. Ribeiro; Bill Byrne; Felix Hieber
method: Benchmarking 5 LLMs on cross-lingual news QA with document relevancy annotations
findings_with_location: Uncovers two challenges: response language correctness in monolingual retrieval; cross-lingual reasoning over retrieved docs in multilingual retrieval (Abstract; Sec 5)
limitations_with_location: Focuses on QA generation rather than claim verification or systematic translation fidelity error attribution
overlap: Benchmark for QA generation across languages; does not analyze claim verification or original vs translated evidence flip attribution

title: Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive Question Answering Task
authors: Leonardo Ranaldi; Barry Haddow; Alexandra Birch
method: Compares tRAG (question translation); MultiRAG (multilingual retrieval); and CrossRAG (translating retrieved documents to English)
findings_with_location: CrossRAG (translating retrieved documents into English before generation) improves QA performance across languages (Abstract; Sec 4)
limitations_with_location: Does not decompose translation error types; does not address claim verification or selective original checking
overlap: Studies translating retrieved documents to English for QA; does not examine claim-verification label flips or verifier reasoning errors
novelty_risk: Moderate-Low (different task; no error decomposition or selective checking)

title: All Languages Matter: Understanding and Mitigating Language Bias in Multilingual RAG
authors: Dan Wang; Guozhao Mo; Yafei Shi; Cheng Zhang; Bo Zheng; Boxi Cao; Xuanang Chen; Yaojie Lu; Hongyu Lin; Ben He; Xianpei Han; Le Sun
method: Identifies language bias in mRAG reranking; proposes LAURA (Language-Agnostic Utility-driven Reranker Alignment)
findings_with_location: Rerankers systematically suppress answer-critical documents in non-English/non-native query languages; LAURA aligns rerankers to utility (Abstract)
limitations_with_location: Addresses retriever/reranker stage only; does not analyze verifier stage or evidence translation fidelity
overlap: Focuses on retrieval and reranking stage; does not study verifier reasoning or evidence translation errors

title: A Comparative Study of Translation Bias and Accuracy in Multilingual Large Language Models for Cross-Language Claim Verification
authors: Aryan Singhal; Veronica Shao; Gary Sun; Ryan Ding; Jonathan Lu; Kevin Zhu
method: Compares direct inference; pre-translation; and self-translation using LLMs and mBERT baseline
findings_with_location: Pre-translation and self-translation improve accuracy over direct inference in low-resource languages; self-translation reduces bias in larger models (Abstract; Sec 4)
limitations_with_location: Treats fact-checking accuracy as a monolithic score; does not isolate translation fidelity from verifier reasoning; no error taxonomy annotation; no selective checking mechanism
overlap: Direct predecessor in cross-lingual claim verification on X-Fact; but leaves open the causal attribution of flips (translation vs verifier reasoning) and does not provide selective checking

title: X-FACT: A New Benchmark Dataset for Multilingual Fact Checking
method: Created 25-language fact-checking benchmark with naturally occurring claims; expert veracity labels; and search evidence snippets
findings_with_location: Multilingual models (mBERT; XLM-R) struggle in zero-shot cross-lingual claim verification; out-of-domain transfer is difficult (Sec 5)
limitations_with_location: Baseline models use flat concatenation of snippets; no controlled translation fidelity study
overlap: Foundational dataset for multilingual claim verification; MIT license

title: When Scale Meets Diversity: Evaluating Language Models on Fine-Grained Multilingual Claim Verification
authors: Hanna Shcharbakova; Tatiana Anikina; Natalia Skachkova; Josef van Genabith
method: Evaluates 5 models (XLM-R; mT5; Llama 3.1; Qwen 2.5; Mistral Nemo) under prompting and fine-tuning
findings_with_location: XLM-R (270M) substantially outperforms 7-12B parameter LLMs (57.7% vs 16.9% macro-F1); LLMs show evidence-utilization failures and majority-class bias (Abstract; Table 2)
limitations_with_location: Does not conduct paired original vs translated evidence error attribution; no selective original-evidence verification
overlap: Closest recent benchmark comparison on X-Fact; confirms evidence utilization is a major challenge for LLMs

title: XFEVER: Exploring Fact Verification across Languages
method: Translates FEVER claims and evidence into 6 languages; evaluates zero-shot and translate-train; calibrates via English-target prediction similarity
findings_with_location: Multilingual models transfer efficiently but remain inferior to English; prediction similarity mitigates miscalibration (Abstract)
limitations_with_location: Synthetic/translated claims and evidence from Wikipedia; does not test real cross-lingual RAG evidence retrieval or selective checking
overlap: Examines translated claims and evidence; does not isolate translation vs reasoning error attribution on real-world news claims
